findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and console to anyone with instance/API describe access, risking credential theft.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data at rest on the volume is stored unencrypted, exposing sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.

The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, so it inherits the lack of encryption and could expose data at rest if the snapshot is copied, shared, or made public.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the instance.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, TLS termination), exposing the web service directly to the internet in plaintext.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive a public IP address, increasing exposure to internet-based attacks especially combined with the permissive security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive a public IP address, increasing exposure to internet-based attacks.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to network traffic metadata.
